security_spec.violation_condition: In QEMU TCG, when a saturating shift-left instruction (PSSLAI.H, PSSLAI.W, SSLAI, PSSHA.DHS, PSSHA.DWS, PSSHAR.DHS, PSSHAR.DWS, PSSLAI.DH, PSSLAI.DW) computes 'a << shamt' in the native element width (e.g., int16_t for halfword, int32_t for word) without widening the intermediate result to at least 2x the element width, causing silent integer overflow before the saturation bounds check executes. The spec requires the comparison 'result < -2^15' and 'result > 2^15-1' to operate on a mathematically-precise shifted value, but a naive TCG implementation using C-level shifts wraps around modulo 2^N, making overflowed values appear non-overflowing and bypassing saturation to produce arbitrary wraparound results. This also applies to the double-wide register-pair variants where the same per-element shift-saturate logic runs on even/odd register pairs — a single-element TCG overflow bug propagates to both halves.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: tcg_gen_shl_i{32,64} or tcg_gen_sari_i{32,64} on packed element without prior sign extension to double-width temporary, followed by signed comparison against saturation bounds — the shift intermediate must be computed at 2× element width before truncation and saturation clamping
security_spec.summary: Saturating left-shift intermediate must be computed at >=2x element width to preserve overflow bits for correct saturation detection; native-width TCG shifts silently wrap before saturation bounds check fires

findings.finding: The P-extension (Zpn/Zpsf) saturating/rounding shift instructions (PSSLAI.H, PSSLAI.W, SSLAI, PSSHA.DHS, PSSHA.DWS, PSSHAR.DHS, PSSHAR.DWS, PSSLAI.DH, PSSLAI.DW) are not implemented in this QEMU codebase. No trans_p*.c.inc files exist, no TCG helper entries for these mnemonics, no decode table entries, and no references to P-extension ISA strings (Zpn, Zpsf) anywhere in target/riscv/. The current branch 'fix-pmp-this-addr-overflow' contains only a PMP integer overflow fix (target/riscv/pmp.c) and an IOMMU validation change (hw/riscv/riscv-iommu.c). Since the P-ext saturating shift code does not exist, the described vulnerability (narrow integer shift before saturation bounds check) cannot be assessed against actual code.
findings.snippet: N/A — no P-ext saturating shift implementation exists in this tree
